tagline: Down the Cle Elum valley through old coal towns to Thorp.
intro: From below Cle Elum Lake, SR 903 runs down the valley of the Cle Elum River through Ronald and Roslyn to Cle Elum, near where the river meets the Yakima. From there SR 970 and SR 10 carry it on east past Teanaway to Thorp. The byway itself starts higher up, at the Salmon La Sac campground, and goes on past Thorp to Ellensburg, so the line drawn here is its middle stretch.
This is old coal and timber country, of company towns, logging camps, mines and ranches, and the corridor takes the back roads past communities that travelers on the speedier bypass miss entirely.

moments.title: Roslyn
moments.text: The coal company town of 1886 buries its dead in 26 adjoining cemetery plots that reflect the many peoples who came to work the mines, and was later a filming location for Northern Exposure.

moments.title: Cle Elum
moments.text: Railroad surveyors named their depot here Clealum in 1886, from the Kittitas Tle-el-Lum, swift water, after the river, and only in 1908 did it come apart into Cle Elum.

moments.title: Thorp Mill
moments.text: From 1907 the 1883 gristmill's water wheel also turned a dynamo, lighting homes a few hours each evening and putting Thorp among the first towns in Washington with electricity.
